title: Computer Networks
tagline: Layers and protocols, the application layer, sockets, reliable transport, TCP and congestion control, IP and routing, link layers and wireless networks
summary: The internet connects billions of devices by layering simple protocols over unreliable links. This course follows the layers from the top down — applications and sockets, reliable transport and TCP congestion control, IP addressing and routing, link layers and switching, wireless and mobile networks — and explains the performance and design principles that let the internet scale.

chapters.title: Networks and layering
chapters.summary: Packet switching, delay, loss and throughput, protocol layers and the architecture of the internet.

chapters.title: The application layer
chapters.summary: The web and HTTP, the domain name system, email and content distribution networks.

chapters.title: Socket programming
chapters.summary: The sockets interface, clients and servers over TCP and UDP, and concurrent servers.

chapters.title: Reliable data transfer
chapters.summary: UDP, the principles of reliable transfer, and stop-and-wait, go-back-N and selective repeat.

chapters.title: TCP and congestion control
chapters.summary: TCP connections and flow control, congestion control from AIMD to modern algorithms, and fairness.

chapters.title: The network layer and IP
chapters.summary: Forwarding, IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, subnetting, network address translation and ICMP.

chapters.title: Routing
chapters.summary: Link-state and distance-vector routing, OSPF, and inter-domain routing with BGP.

chapters.title: The link layer and local networks
chapters.summary: Error detection, multiple access, Ethernet, switches and virtual LANs.

chapters.title: Wireless and mobile networks
chapters.summary: Wi-Fi and cellular networks, mobility, and the effect of wireless links on transport protocols.
